review_scope: Assistant desk review of cited source text and exact ESCO skill relationships. Not independent human validation, UN endorsement or measured occupational impact.

links.reason: Solar PV systems create end-of-life waste, while collection, reuse and recycling can reduce that burden. IRENA/IEA-PVPS documents this technology-level trade-off. It is not evidence that a particular engineer causes harm or manages recycling, nor an estimate of Malaysia's current waste.

context_sources.label: IRENA / IEA-PVPS, End-of-Life Management: Solar Photovoltaic Panels (June 2016), executive summary
context_sources.quote: Sustainable end-of-life management policies for PV panels can be achieved through an enabling regulatory framework, along with the institutions needed to implement it.

Providing professional nursing care is an essential ESCO activity. It relates to access to essential health-care services in target 3.8, not proof of universal access or financial protection.
ESCO describes treating water for safe drinking and lists water-quality measurement as essential. This addresses safe-water provision, not proof of affordable or equitable access.

ESCO describes designing systems that generate electricity from sunlight and lists solar energy as essential. This relates to renewable-energy production, not an observed change in Malaysia's energy mix.
ESCO describes designing renewable-energy production systems and lists wind energy as essential. This is an activity-to-target association, not measured renewable deployment.
